name: Sculpfun E1 Pro 21W
tagline: Enclosed 21W CoreXY diode with camera and air pump included, IR module optional
tldr: The Sculpfun E1 Pro puts a 21W diode on a CoreXY gantry inside a Class 1 enclosure with a 400 × 320 mm work area, built-in camera, air pump and honeycomb bed. Sculpfun claims 600 mm/s engraving and 12 mm wood in one pass. A Dual bundle adds a swappable 3W 1064 nm IR module for metal. Launched June 2026; no in-depth independent review yet.
mainObjective: Enclosed diode engraving and wood cutting on a mid-size bed at an open-frame price

priceRange.note: $849 single 21W, $1,149 Dual with 3W IR module (Sculpfun store, Oct 2026)

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood & plywood up to 12 mm (claimed, one pass)
cannot: Objects taller than 42 mm (30 mm with honeycomb)

pros: Class 1 enclosure with lid sensor, emergency stop and safety key at an open-frame price
21W on a CoreXY gantry: fast engraving and serious diode cutting in the same box
Camera, air pump and honeycomb bed included, with nothing to assemble
Swappable 3W IR module (Dual bundle or $499 add-on) marks bare metal and plastics
cons: Only 30 mm of clearance with the honeycomb (42 mm without): no tumblers without a riser
New model: cutting claims are Sculpfun's, no in-depth independent review yet
beginnerNotes: This profile is the E1 Pro (21W) in the Sculpfun E1 line. Compare it with the 12W E1: choose the E1 Pro if you plan to cut wood regularly. The Dual bundle is worth it only if you want to mark bare metal: the IR module can also be bought later.
proTips: Keep the air pump on for every cut and check focus with the gauge before each job, since there is no auto-focus. For tall objects, remove the honeycomb or add the metal risers Sculpfun sells for the E1 series. Vent the exhaust outside or add the SP1 purifier.

faq.question: What is the difference between the Sculpfun E1 and E1 Pro?
faq.answer: Same enclosure, CoreXY gantry, 400 × 320 mm work area and camera. The E1 has a 12W diode (8 mm wood per pass claimed), the E1 Pro a 21W diode (12 mm claimed). The E1 Pro costs $350 more.

faq.question: What does the Dual version add?
faq.answer: A 3W 1064 nm infrared module that swaps with the diode head. It marks bare metals (stainless, gold, silver, aluminum) and plastics with a 0.03 mm spot. It is also sold separately for $499.

faq.question: Can the E1 Pro cut clear acrylic?
faq.answer: No. Like every blue diode, it passes through clear acrylic. Dark and opaque acrylic can be cut in thin sheets; clear acrylic needs a CO₂ laser.

editorialDepth.advantages: The E1 Pro brings 21W cutting power into a closed Class 1 box for well under $1,000, with camera and air pump included. The CoreXY gantry is built for speed, and the 400 × 320 mm area covers most signs, boxes and batches of coasters.
editorialDepth.limitations: Clearance is shallow (30 mm with the honeycomb), focus is manual, and the 12 mm cutting figure is a manufacturer claim. Clear acrylic remains out of reach, as with any diode.
